Thanks Marcus — quick operational notes from Marketplace side:

1) Marketplace can issue "cohort top-up" vouchers scoped to a publisher listing but there are two constraints: the top-up must be tied to a partner tag (Streetlight) and we need an authorization email from the Redwood rep + an MOU for any expiry changes beyond the marketplace standard.

2) We can create 300 promo codes equating to ~30k token credits and set a 30 day expiry extension on the new codes. Existing codes already issued by the Marketplace cannot be retroactively extended; only newly issued codes can have the 30-day window.

3) Ops will need one of the following to proceed:
   - Signed MOU (simple 1-page) with Streetlight, or
   - Written approval from Revenue/Finance for a one-off promo: discount/credit policy waiver.

I recommend the MOU route — faster for partner trust. I'll draft the MOU and attach for sign-off. Once signed, Marketplace Ops can generate and push the codes to Samir within 24 business hours.

Agree with the MOU approach. A few compliance and finance checks:

- Promo top-up of the scale requested (30k tokens across cohort) is within allowable partner subsidy thresholds for pilot programs under our current channel policy, provided we: 
  a) capture expected outcomes (activation rate, follow-on ARR signal), and
  b) limit redemption to the partner-tagged vouchers.

- Legal will need a signed MOU (simple sponsor letter) confirming Streetlight will not re-sell vouchers and that they’ll report usage monthly for 90 days. Vanessa — if you can add the two clauses above to the draft, Finance will approve the one-off.

- Also recommend we provision the promo codes with a usage cap per code (e.g., 100 tokens) to avoid a single account consuming the whole allocation.

If you can circulate the editable MOU link (DocuSign preferred), I'll sign off within the day.

Thanks — Priya
